0 = one soft pulse. 1 = a sharp lub, then a clearly separate softer dub. Derives the knock timing and intensity split automatically — see lowHealthTexture if you want those set by hand instead.
1 = every scripted event, 3 = only the most severe. Higher means rarer, more significant warnings.
A bright tick when you learn a new ability.
A crisp mechanical snap on the high motor.
A dry click when you use an ability that has no cast time.
A heavy, decisive impact when your current target dies.
A light click when a major UI panel is dismissed.
A light click when the last confirmation dialog closes.
A light tick when you step away from an NPC or close its window.
A ringing anvil strike when repairing armor and weapons at a vendor.
A rising celebratory surge when you gain a level.
A sharp alert pulse when your hostile target or focus turns to target you.
A sharp deflection tick when a cast of yours is rejected outright — out of range, not facing the target, still on cooldown.
A sharp deflection tick when the game refuses an action — out of range, facing the wrong way, not enough resource, still on cooldown.
A sharp snap when a harmful effect lands on you.
A sharp snap with a short tail.
A short warning before a significant scripted boss ability, using Blizzard's own built-in Boss Warnings timeline.
A short, sharp tick instead of the normal one when the segment you land on can't be used.
A single dry click, lighter than a tick.
A single very short, very hard hit.
A slow low/high oscillation — the caller supplies the phase.
A soft tick followed by a brighter one.
A soft tick when releasing the group targeting modifier back to normal navigation.
A soft tick when you cancel a radial selection instead of committing to it.
A soft tick when you start auto-attacking with a ranged weapon (Auto Shot, Shoot, wands).
A soft tick when you start meleeing.
A soft tick when you start resting in an inn or major city.
A soft tick when your melee auto-attack stops — catches walking out of range or a target dying without noticing.
A steady, stronger texture — meant to be scaled by the caller (e.g. speed).
A tactile micro-tick each time the stack splitter quantity slider changes.
A tactile recoil kick on every Auto Shot arrow, timed to the real shot, not estimated.
A tap when a confirmation dialog opens.
A tap when an NPC or world object opens a window nothing else here covers.
A texture that builds as your gliding speed climbs toward a boost.
A tick when a book, plaque, gravestone or signpost opens to be read.
A tick when a piece of your gear's durability drops into the low or broken range.
A tiny blip when you gain experience.
A tiny low blip, for things that happen often.
A triumphant dual-tone chime when you earn an achievement.
A very light tick per combo point, building toward a full resource.
A very light tick when your equipped gear changes.
A very short, sharp tick when you avoid an incoming attack.
Adjust your global master vibration strength. Individual cues can always be fine-tuned in settings.
Also fires when you cancel a cast yourself, or move out of range — it means "your cast did not finish", not specifically "you were kicked".
Also fires when you switch to a target that is already mid-cast.
Alternates between the motors — an unsteady, rolling feel.
Alternating low thud and high snap across motors.
Applies only while this character is in this specialization. Switching specialization switches profile with it, with no further action from you.
Applies to this character whatever specialization it is in. This is the rule the profile picker on the Pulse page has always written to.
Attentive triage. Emergency low health warnings, dispel/CC alerts, kick warnings, and heal completion confirmation with subdued personal damage.
Automatically switch to %s whenever this character is in this specialization.

Bends the relationship between what a cue asks for and what the motor is told. Below 1.0 makes quiet cues louder; above 1.0 makes them quieter and reserves more of the range for strong ones. 1.0 is the unbent default.
Builds from a low hum into a high pulse.
Cast texture, cast finish confirmation, lockout/pushback warnings, proc glows, kick alerts
Choose the addon display language. Automatic follows the game client. Missing translations use English. Changes apply after /reload.
Climbs this motor slowly from silence to %d%% power over %d seconds,
Configure tactile rewards for exploring Azeroth and sensory spatial awareness for targeting.
Copy "%s" to a new custom profile named:
Copy "%s" to a new profile named:
Create a new editable custom profile that starts as an exact copy of %s.
Create a new profile from Registry.lua's stock defaults and switch to it.
Create a new profile that starts as an exact copy of the one in use, and switch to it. The two are independent from the first edit.
Delete profile "%s"? This can't be undone.
Disable every vibration cue in the active profile in one sweep for quiet testing or building a profile from scratch.
Displays a shortcut button on the edge of your minimap for quick access to settings and toggling vibration.
Distinguished from cancelling by Blizzard's own `isCancelled` flag, which it sets before ending the selection — so a cancel never counts as a choice.
Doubles as the catch-all: a loss-of-control type this addon does not recognise — a new one added by a patch — fires this generic cue instead of being silently dropped.
Dual asymmetrical ERM motors, balanced 75ms spin-up
Enable every vibration cue in the active profile in one sweep for testing and debugging.
Evoker-only in practice. It stays registered for every class and simply never fires for the others.
Fast attack time constant used specifically for discrete impacts, clicks, and strikes. Gives snappy transients without making sustained immersion textures harsh.
Fires as an empowered cast of yours begins and ends.
Fires for any summon confirmation dialog, not only a player summoning you.
Fires on input, so it also fires for casts that then fail. That is intentional: this is an input-acknowledgement cue, not a success cue.
Fires on the change itself, not on every flag update.
Fires on the crossing into low, not repeatedly while low.
Fires on the yellow informational messages the game shows in the top centre of the screen.
Fires only when a queue enters the ready-to-enter state, not on every status update.
Fires the instant you press a cast, before the server has confirmed it.
Fires upon arrival at destination when player control is restored.
Fires when a battleground or arena queue is ready to enter.
Fires when a boss encounter begins.
Fires when a boss encounter ends, in victory or in a wipe.
Fires when a flight master's map opens.
Fires when a loading screen ends and the world is back.
Fires when a quest is handed in and its reward is taken.
Fires when a quest's completion page opens, ready to hand in.
Fires when a quest's detail page opens, ready to accept.
Fires when a ready check completes or times out.
Fires when a ready check starts.
Fires when a role check starts.
Fires when a trade window opens.
Fires when a vendor window opens.
Fires when an innkeeper asks to make this your home.
Fires when gaining money with an open vendor window.
Fires when group leadership changes hands.
Fires when one of your own casts begins.
Fires when one of your own casts completes successfully — distinct from a cast simply ending.
Fires when one of your own casts ends, whether or not it completed.
Fires when someone challenges you to a duel.
Fires when someone invites you to a group.
Fires when someone joins or leaves your group.
Fires when someone offers you a resurrection and the accept dialog appears.
Fires when someone summons you and the accept dialog appears.
Fires when spending money with an open vendor window.
Fires when the stable master's window opens.
Fires when you accept a quest.
Fires when you are confused or possessed (CONFUSE, POSSESS).
Fires when you are feared or charmed (FEAR, FEAR_MECHANIC, CHARM).
Fires when you are resurrected or leave ghost form.
Fires when you are rooted in place (ROOT). You can still act, so this is a rung below the cues that stop you entirely.
Fires when you are stunned (STUN, STUN_MECHANIC).
Fires when you change target, including when you clear it.
Fires when you enter a new zone.
Fires when you enter a vehicle and your action bar is replaced.
Fires when you leave a vehicle and your own action bar returns.
Fires when you set or clear your focus target.
Fires when your class's secondary resource fills up — combo points, holy power, soul shards, chi, arcane charges, essence or runes, whichever your specialisation uses.
Fires when your focus target begins casting.
Fires when your own away or do-not-disturb flag actually changes.
Gentle steady engine-like cruise vibration while riding flight master gryphons, bats, or wyverns.
Heavy left counterweight (85ms), light right counterweight (45ms)
How far the hum swells either side of its baseline. 0 is a flat hold.
How fast the wingbeat-style undulation cycles.
How many seconds before the scripted moment this fires.

How pronounced each stroke is against its own baseline. Higher values (0.80-1.0) allow the counterweight to physically spin down during the glide phase between strokes. 0 is a flat drag with no rhythm at all.
How steady the low motor stays regardless of speed. Only audible while actually gliding.
How strong the hum gets by the moment a regular cast completes. Only audible if "Casting texture" is also enabled on its own tab.
Immediately switch to %s for the current character.
Initial software voltage boost applied during transient onset to accelerate the motor rapidly to target speed. 1.0 is disabled.
Leave this scope with no opinion and let the next one decide.
Low motor holds a steady presence, floored so it's never silent while gliding; high motor eases in from near-silent toward thrillPeak as speed climbs, shaped by thrillCurve.
Master switch for every loss-of-control cue below. With this off, none of them fire and no loss-of-control events are registered at all.
Master switch. With this off, nothing registers and nothing costs anything.
Most specific wins. A scope set to |cffffd100No rule|r has no opinion and lets the one below it decide; with none of them set, Pulse uses Default.
Multiplies every trigger's intensity. Part of the current profile, not global.
ON — option changes and cue firings will print here.
Ocean zones only (guessed from zone name)
Off by default and deliberately the faintest cue in the addon: this fires for EVERY NPC you talk to, which in a city is constantly. Try it before leaving it on. Untested.
One cue for both directions, same reasoning as the navigation edge cue — a motor can't tell you which way you went.
One full-bodied hit on both motors.
One long, sombre pulse when a spirit healer's window opens.
One sharp, heavy impact — fast attack, fast decay.
Overall heave amplitude of the oceanic swell. Sets the physical displacement intensity of the slow motor.

Overall strength. Meant to sit at the edge of perception — if you notice it as a vibration rather than as being submerged, it is too high. Inherits the old idleFloatAmplitude, which was live-tuned to 0.04.
PLAYER_ALIVE also fires when you release to a graveyard, so this can fire while you are still a ghost.

PLAYER_SOFT_FRIEND_CHANGED, occurrence-only, no payload. Worth pairing with the hostile cue above only if you can tell two TICKs apart — if not, give one of them a different shape with its own "Feels like" dropdown.
Passively polled by observing IsEnabled() on the currently focused element. Fires if the element becomes disabled while focused.
Passively polled via GetUIPanel every 0.05s to eliminate UIParentPanelManager execution taint on protected frames.
Passively polled via GetUIPanel every 0.05s. Detects when major UI panels are dismissed without callback taint.
Passively polled via GroupTargeting.isTargetingActive. Fires when the group targeting modifier is released.
Physical tool strikes: anvil hammer strokes, mining pickaxe impacts, tailoring stitches.
Pick a mode to test below.
Play a few seconds of this texture at its current intensity. Module-driven preview reproducing authentic physical dynamics and configured intensity.

Prints every option you change and every cue that actually fires to chat, in real time. Same as /pulse debug — off by default, and resets to off on /reload since it's a testing aid, not a saved preference.
Progressive low build leading to a sharp high break.
Pulse is using |cffffd100%s|r, because a rule is set for %s.
Pulse tunes motor spin-up attack, coast-down release, and breakaway friction to match your physical hardware actuators.

Pure flavour — nothing depends on it. Untested.
Pure novelty. Off by default forever, basically — nobody asked for this one.
Put every motor's strength, floor, timing and curve back to the engine defaults. Doesn't touch cues, per-cue intensity, mode tuning or your schema.
Put the profile in use back to its stock defaults — works on built-ins too, restoring their curated content rather than blank Registry.lua defaults.
Rapid staccato triple-click on the high motor.
Reads the segment's own IsEnabled() — the same value Blizzard reads to grey the highlight out, so this matches what you see on screen. Fires in place of "Radial segment changed", not alongside it.
Reload UI to apply the language change.
Reload the interface to apply your selected addon language.
Rename the profile in use. Every rule pointing at it follows the rename. Built-in profiles can't be renamed.
Reset every motor's strength, floor, timing and curve back to the engine defaults? This can't be undone.
Reset profile "%s" to defaults? Every cue, intensity and mode override in it goes back to stock values. This can't be undone.
Same polled mechanism as "Confirmation popup appeared". Untested.
Scales both the bed and the strikes for %s, before the two shared strengths above.
Scales this cue on top of the overall intensity on the Pulse page.
School lockouts are frequent in melee-heavy content. Off by default because a cue every kick you eat can crowd out the ones that mean you cannot act at all.
Set but not in force: |cffffd100%s|r. A more specific rule above is winning — clear it to let these take over.
Shares its pulse pattern with the target cue. If your focus is also your target, you get one cue rather than two.
Sharp high kick layered with heavy low kick and rumble decay.
Show a Play button on every cue
Shows only the page switches and this page. Every cue keeps its own settings; turn this off to get every page back exactly as it was.
Slow, harmonic oceanic gravity swells and coastal tides while submerged in deep oceans.
Steps per second at full running speed. Scaled by how fast you are actually moving.
Steps per second at normal walking speed.
Strokes per second at barely-moving speed.
Switches every cue on the Casting page on or off at once. Each cue keeps its own setting underneath.
Switches every cue on the Character & Status page on or off at once. Each cue keeps its own setting underneath.
Switches every cue on the Interface & Accessibility page on or off at once. Each cue keeps its own setting underneath.
Switches every cue on the Movement & Travel page on or off at once. Each cue keeps its own setting underneath.
Switches every cue on the Social & Group page on or off at once. Each cue keeps its own setting underneath.
Switches every cue on the Target & Focus page on or off at once. Each cue keeps its own setting underneath.
Switches every cue on the World & Environment page on or off at once. Each cue keeps its own setting underneath.
The _QUIET variant covers failures the game prints no error for, so this can fire with nothing visible on screen.
The lightest possible tick when a conversation window opens with any NPC.
The master switch for this page. Also on the Casting page, where the cue lives alongside the other casting cues.
This character reports no specialization, so there is no per-specialization rule to set. The row appears by itself on a character that has one.
Three-stage rising tension building on the low motor.
Time in seconds for a complete wave cycle. Real oceanic swells roll every 8 to 12 seconds (~0.10 Hz). Shorter periods feel like choppy coastal chop; longer periods feel like open-ocean rollers.
Tuned for HD Rumble voice-coil actuators
Turn off every cue in the active profile in one sweep (useful for quiet debugging).
Turn on every cue in the active profile in one sweep (useful for testing/debugging).
Turn whole pages of cues on or off. Each cue keeps its own setting underneath: switching a page back on restores exactly what was there.
Two crisp ticks when a cooldown the built-in Cooldown Manager is tracking comes off cooldown.
Two heavier hits with a gap between them.
Two kinds of trigger: pulses and textures
Two soft ticks when the action bar pages to a different set of abilities.
Two soft ticks when you page the radial left or right with the shoulder buttons.

Untested whether this also fires on every instant-cast press rather than only real cast-bar completions — if so, it'll feel far too frequent to read as "that landed" specifically. Check before relying on it.
Voice-coil actuators (LRA), ultra-low 0.025 floor, instant response
Watches UNIT_TARGET and target swaps for hostile units whose target is the player. Uses UnitIsUnit('targettarget', 'player') with defensive secrecy guards.
When mobs are pulled socially — aggroing because a neighbour was pulled — the game often reports status 0 even though you have aggro.
Which of the preset shapes this specific cue plays when it fires. "
Which physical motors each cue drives. Start with Standard Rumble, then calibrate the motors below.
Which physical motors each trigger drives. Try one, test a mode below, keep the one you can feel.

Which profile to use right now. This writes to whichever rule is currently in force, so picking here always changes what you are actually using rather than editing a rule something more specific is overriding.
Wind resistance & thrust surge while flying. Scales dynamically with your flight speed.
